description: We are MADA | مدى, a student team participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We are passionate about space exploration, coding, and using technology to solve challenges. We welcome motivated members interested in web development, 3D visualization, data analysis, and planetary science. Experience is a plus, but curiosity, creativity, and teamwork matter most. Join us and explore beyond the horizon!
summary:
MADA (Mars Astronaut Decision Assistant) is a web-based prototype that explores how Martian terrain data can support surface exploration planning. Focusing on Gale Crater, we developed an interface for comparing routes by distance, terrain difficulty, and scientific interest, alongside an elevation-data processing workflow and a slope-analysis script using NASA MOLA data.

MADA addresses the challenge by connecting planetary information with an understandable planning experience. Its goal is to explain exploration trade-offs rather than simply display the shortest path. The current routes and comparison metrics are illustrative; terrain-based route calculation was not fully integrated and validated.

By making complex data more accessible, MADA aims to help students, educators, and space enthusiasts understand both the opportunities and limitations of planning journeys across Mars. It provides a foundation for future data-driven route comparisons, not an operational astronaut navigation system.
details:
MADA (Mars Astronaut Decision Assistant) is a web-based prototype designed to make Mars exploration planning easier to understand. Focusing on Gale Crater, it demonstrates how users could compare routes based on distance, terrain difficulty, and scientific interest.

We built the interface using JavaScript, React, Vite, Leaflet, and CSS, with Node.js and Express for backend development. We also prepared a MOLA elevation grid and developed a slope-analysis script. The displayed routes and metrics remain illustrative; terrain-based route calculation was not fully integrated and validated.

MADA’s creative approach is to explain exploration trade-offs rather than simply display the shortest route. It aims to help students, educators, and space enthusiasts explore planetary data through an accessible interface.

Our team considered data resolution, geographic alignment, missing information, computing limitations, and responsible communication of uncertainty. MADA is an educational demonstration, not an operational navigation system.
